The repeated coordinate columns force exactly \(2^k\) parity-compatible major arcs, all with the same phase; bounded columns and positive-definite covariance give the Gaussian local limit. Multiplying the probability by the \(2^{T+k}\) initial sign vectors reproduces the constant and offset exponent. A fresh dynamic program independently reproduced representative exact counts for \(k=2,3\) and their convergence toward the predicted constants.
